newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Ex-minister named Trinidad central bank governor.
newsitem.headline: Ex-minister named Trinidad central bank governor.

text.p: Former government minister Winston Dookeran began work Friday as the new governor of the Trinidad and Tobago Central Bank.
Dookeran's appointment was announced and approved by the cabinet Thursday, officials said. He replaced the retiring Ainsworth Harewood.
Prior to his appointment, Dookeran, 54, worked as a senior economist at the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC).
He was Minister of Planning and Mobilization from 1986 to 1991 and acted as prime minister following the 1990 coup attempt by a group of armed black muslims.
A graduate of the London School of Economics before entering politics in 1981, Dookeran also was a lecturer at the University of the West Indies.
Peter July, managing director of Royal Bank, described Dookeran as "experienced, well qualified, and recognized in financial circles in and outside Trinidad and Tobago."

"I am confident the new governor will receive the full support and commitment from the local banking community," he added. Former Finance Minister Wendell Mottley was also considered for the job, according to television reports.
